vocabulary.definition: A "high roller" is a slang word for someone who spends huge amounts of money to enjoy their lives. High rollers buy expensive wines, awesome sports cars, boats, and even possibly personal airplanes. Sometimes we use this word to describe friends who spend more than most others in the group. Often these people are very generous with their money and enjoy treating their friends to stuff.
This is a slang phrase that means to "earn a lot of money". For the first few years his business was struggling but now he's making some serious bank.

If something is "all show" it kind of implies that it's a bit fake. In the dialog, the guy who was spending a lot of money didn't really have the money. Other people who saw him would think he was rich but the truth was he was using the money from his credit cards. This is all show because it looks cool but the reality is quite different.

If you "ring up" a huge debt or a huge bill it means that you've been buying a lot of things that you still haven't been paid for. You are spending money very quickly and will get a big bill soon. I rang up a huge cell phone bill last month. I had no idea how much the drinks were at that bar. I guess we somehow rang up a $3000 tab last night. ww.china232.com

If you "max out" on your credit card it means that you spent the maximum amount of money you are allowed to spend and now you are no longer allowed to spend any more money until you pay some of it off.
If you "rip through" something it means you use it up very quickly. The new speed boat really rips through gas. It costs over 2 dollars a minute worth of gas to drive it.

A "Start up" is a short for of a "start up company". This is the kind of company that probably got some money from investors to make the business grow. This company is probably not profitable yet but they have potential.
If you make your money back "and then some" it means you get your original investment back plus more.

This is a very common way of saying that a new product is starting to be sold in stores. Stores have "shelves" and when a new product is launched in a store we call it "hitting the shelves". I'm going to buy a second generation Ipad as soon as it hits the shelves in Shanghai.
